BiblicalUsage: mârûwd is an outcast, and in the abstract, destitution itself. In Isaiah 58:7 the fast God chooses is to bring the poor who are cast out to your house, and to cover the naked and not hide from your own flesh. In Lamentations 1:7 Jerusalem remembers her pleasant things in the days of her affliction and miseries, and in Lamentations 3:19 the prophet remembers his own affliction and misery, the wormwood and the gall. The word is the person with nowhere to go.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârûwd shows me that the outcast belongs at my table. I hold that the house that takes in the poor cast out is the house God blesses.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
